utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Laurie Sartorio for the Prosecution and Matthias Neuner, and our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends from the Prosecution, to everyone in and around the courtroom. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Nicholas Robson, I appear here on behalf of General Delic's Defence, together with Lana Deljkic, who is our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Sir, may I just remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made yesterday at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you very much. Madam Sartorio, may I remind you this is a 92 ter witness and we should finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I appreciate that, and I did spend some time last night. I would like, with the Court's indulgence, a short period of time just to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How short is short?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thirty minutes, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, that is too much. Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a very important witness and it's our crime base in September; and, you know, if things didn't go smoothly yesterday, I apologise for that. That's was my fault, but the case shouldn't suffer. All I want to do this morning, Your Honour, is just link the documents that were shown yesterday to paragraphs in the indictment, and I'll go as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like the witness to be shown the statement, the statement of June of 2000, which was marked for identification 643, please. If he could be shown paragraph 33. No, that's October. Please, June of 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If we can zoom in to this statement, we can hardly read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: 643. It should be the June. That's not the correct statement, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI 644, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Paragraph 33, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, in this paragraph, you refer to a handwritten list of names, dated 11 September, 1995, that you had received from an ICTY investigator. You also state in this paragraph that the list had been made, according to you, by an ABiH soldier and that it contained the names of VRS soldiers who had been detained at Kesten. I just want to make it clear, by this list, that -- is this the list, the handwritten list, that was shown to you yesterday in court? Can you answer that question? Remember you looked at a handwritten list yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters are interpreting.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the list we were looking at yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you could look at paragraph 38, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we zoom in?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, in this paragraph, you also refer to the Kesten list; and I just want it clear for the record, is this the same document with the handwritten names?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Allow me a second to go through it. On the list, we were looking at yesterday that is handwritten, there are names of people who used to belong to the 4th Ozren Brigade, and we had received that list from their home unit. By comparing that to the list written by hand, we found certain names of certain people who had been reported as missing from that unit. Also on that list, in addition to the 4th Ozren Brigade soldiers, there were other people who were -- did not belong to the 4th Ozren Brigade but were part of the missing persons list, since they were captured at Kesten.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. The point that I'm trying to ask you is: When you refer in your statement to the Kesten list, are you referring to that handwritten list of names that was shown to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like the witness to be shown paragraph 19, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, could you please take a look at paragraph 19, and then I will ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know what it's about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you refer to a grave that was located at the Gostovici River near Kamenica, and I just want to make it clear that these -- and you discuss six of seven persons that were bodies. I want to clarify whether these are the same bodies that we talked about yesterday, with regard to the ICMP DNA records, and also with regard to the index cards for missing persons. Does this paragraph relate to those documents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the bodies from the mass grave that were identified by the DNA method. We looked into some those cards yesterday, and those people are also on the handwritten list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. In paragraph 41 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Please, may the witness be shown 41.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In paragraph 41, sir, you use the phrase "Kamenica grave," I believe, at least that is how it's translated. And then in 43, down below, you also refer to -- well, you refer to "Kamenica grave." In paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May we look at paragraph 36?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I believe in 36, sir --?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: If we can see the English, please. You have to go to the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In 36, you refer to "mass grave near Kamenica." And in paragraph 19 that you just looked at, it says "a grave at Gostovici River near Kamenica." So can you tell the Judges, is this -- when you refer to this gravesite in different ways, "Kamenica grave, "mass grave near Kamenica," "grave at Gostovici River," is this all the same grave that you're talking about, and is it the grave we were talking about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the same grave which is located in Kamenica, next to the River Gostovici, some five or six metres away. We refer to it as the Kamenica grave at the Gostovici River. It is the same grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in paragraphs 41 and 42 --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness -- would you scroll up for a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Again, if you look at 41 and 42, again, we're talking about the Kamenica grave and DNA samples, and my question to you is: Again, so we can focus on these paragraphs, are these the paragraphs that we talked about yesterday with regard to the DNA records?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this document may be put away, and one more document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Hold on, Ms. Sartorio. There's something that caught my eye. Can we scroll up to paragraph 19. Sir, paragraph 19 includes a piece of information which you may not be able to explain, but I just wanted to ask you, nevertheless. If you see a little down in paragraph 19, you say that: "We have confirmed that six of these seven persons were VRS soldiers captured by the ABiH and handed over to the Mujahedin at Kesten." Do you know if this is a correct explanation of how these people ended up in the hands of the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to a statement of a witness -- or rather, the witnesses that survived, we know that some people were held captive in a hall at Kesten. We also know that that group was turned over to the El Mujahedin unit, and they ended up at the Gostovici camp. Yesterday, we saw the photographs of people taken prisoner at Kesten. Those photographs were taken at Gostovici. That was one of the sources. In my operative work, I learned from several different sources that those people who were captured at Kesten, some 50 of them, were handed over to the El Mujahedin unit. As I said in the statement, I don't know whether they were captured by the 2nd or 3rd Corps of the ABiH, but however we do know that they were handed over to the El Mujahedin. Those information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. So just to be sure, they were not captured by the Mujahedin originally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the stories and statements of those who survived, they were taken prisoners by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The witnesses do not know whether it was the 2nd or the 3rd Corps, but it was the ABiH, in any case, not the El Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. We can then move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. May the witness now be shown Exhibit 646, please, which is the list of names, and could we start with the top name, please. Thank you. The first page, the first page in -- yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, sir --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: If we could enlarge it a tad bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to you look at this list, and go down the list and tell me the first person that you see on this list that was identified -- the body was identified from the Kamenica grave. Give us the number and the name, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan Radojcic, number 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And according to the records, is the spelling of this name -- is this the correct name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, I worked with 5.000 names. I don't know whether it was Radovan or Radenko. It is almost the same, and I'm afraid to make a mistake here. Perhaps that could be compared with the list of the missing that I forwarded to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, we're not going to look at the other documents, but what I'm trying to ask you is: You made certain alterations to some names on this list, and you did that according to records that you --

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you made those changes, what were the criteria for the items that you looked at in order to come to the conclusion that the name was changed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The criterion was my database at my office, because it is credible for several reasons. First of all, families reported on their missing members with correct data, correct date of birth, first and last name, and other information. Another criterion was a report of these people's home unit, which was authentic. The third source was the ICRC database, which is also credible and authentic. That is why there was some changes compared to this list. Some names were changed to a certain degree: Dragomir or Dragutin. Based on this list of 51, we entered some changes, and we forwarded the index cards of these people as well as the addresses of their families.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before this list was corrected by you, how had it been generated and by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This list looked exactly the way we see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Listen to my question: How had it been generated before you corrected it, and by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who created the document. I received it from an investigator of this Tribunal. I was told that it comes from a soldier of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I don't know who drafted this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll have a witness testify to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And then, just quickly, who is the next person on this list that you recognise as being one of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next person is Bozidar Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And that's number 10?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, number 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us the next person?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 16, Cedo Dabic, born 1952 in Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, can you go to the next person? And if you have to go to the next page, just please say so.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 18, it reads "Obrad Petrovic." Instead, it should be "Petrusic." This person was found and identified, but not at the Kamenica gravesite. That was the body I mentioned specifically yesterday as having been found some 500 metres from that location, Obrad Petrusic. And then we can move on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Stjepanovic, Drago, or rather, Drago Stjepanovic, number 23. I apologise. There may be certain mistakes in the last name, since we have same or very similar last names between people. I'm speaking from memory. I forwarded all of the names of those identified and even the statements of family members who signed and confirmed that that person had been identified, Drago Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you see anyone others on the list?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise if I omit any names, but it's very difficult for me to speak about every single name, especially if you bear in mind that I had to go through 5.000 names. Mistakes are possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I'm just asking from your memory. If you don't remember, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. One moment, Your Honour, and I'll be finished. May I have one moment? Thank you. Your Honour, I have no further questions, and thank you for your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes. Is it you, Mr. Robson? Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Krcmar. I appear on behalf of General Delic, and I'm going to be asking you some questions this morning. What I'll do is I'll be taking you through your statements and also your testimony that you gave yesterday. Could you please confirm, at the outset, that during the war in 1993, you were appointed a member of the Exchange Commission of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And you've told us in April 1996 you started to work for the Republika Srpska Missing Persons Commission, which is a civilian body?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a governmental institution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, just for my own clarification, when you say the witness was appointed a member of the Exchange Commission of the 1st Krajina Corps, is the 1st Krajina Corps an army unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can you answer that, Mr. Krcmar? Is the 1st Krajina Corps an army unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Krajina Corps is one of the corps of the Army of Republika Srpska. We've been also discussing the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm just trying to be careful about distinguishing between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, thank you. Thank you very much. That was going to be my next question, which army, and now we know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krcmar. I'd like to take you to your statement of June 2007. At paragraph 9, you talk about two VRS officers that were found in 1998, and they told you that sometime before their capture, around an area described as "Pejanovici," they saw a bus containing captured VRS soldiers heading from Kesten towards the direction of Stog. Do you remember mentioning that in your state statement? Do you remember mentioning that, Mr. Krcmar?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and I remember which officers are in question. I know about the whole situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps, if you're able to answer simply "yes" or "no" to my questions, if you're able to do so, I would encourage you to do that. Now, in your statement, you'd agree with me that you are just simply recalling what you were told by the two soldiers back in 1998?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you mean the statement in that paragraph or in the whole statement? Is the whole statement recalling what he was told by the two guys, or is it that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm focusing on paragraph number 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But, you say: "Now in your statement, you would agree with me that you are just simply recalling what you were told by the two soldiers back in 1998." You're saying "statement," so I just want to be clear. Is it the entire statement or is it just paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, paragraph 9 contains information that was relayed to you by the two soldiers; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You don't know when the two soldiers were supposed to have seen this bus, do you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. One needs to read the last sentence of paragraph 9, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And you'd agree with me that you don't know the identities of the men who were supposed to be on that bus?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were captured, according to the statements of the two captured officers. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The question I asked you is: You don't know the identities of the men who were supposed to be on that bus?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, in your statement, you've mentioned the name of the two -- the names of the two soldiers that gave you this information. It's true, isn't it, that the Office of the Prosecution could have interviewed those men with a view to obtaining a statement directly as to what they saw?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to a different subject, and this is the grave that you have referred to as the "Kamenica grave." You'd agree with me that this grave was by the Gostovic River at about the 15 Kilometre location; is that right? That would be 15 kilometres from Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And this grave was opened, and investigations took place on the 21st to the 23rd of June, 2006; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And according to paragraph 19 of your statement of June 2007, the persons carrying out the exhumation at the grave reported finding eight persons? And it's paragraph 19 I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we be shown paragraph 19, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So if we can enlarge paragraph 19 in the B/C/S version, it's in the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Mr. Krcmar, that the -- it was reported that the remains of eight persons were found at that grave?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You were not at that exhumation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's right to say that the first time that you saw the remains of the bodies was in Visoko, when the autopsy took place?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know, were photographs taken of the location where the bodies were found?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know I saw the photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when you were in Visoko, at the autopsy, it's correct that the bodies were brought in contained in separate sealed plastic bags; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to deal with one aspect of your evidence that is rather confusing. In paragraph 42 of your statement, and perhaps if we can bring that paragraph up on the screen, what you say about the bodies is that the police marked the bodies starting at number 1, and then you say: "At Kamenica, they were 1 through 8 bodies."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if we can find that, it's the first two sentences of paragraph 42.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, as I understood your statement, the eight bodies that came from the mass grave were labelled as "1/1," "1/2," "1/3," through to "1/8"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where do you see the "/1"?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that information is not contained in this statement, but it would appear to be the case from other material that's been provided to the Defence. This is what I'm trying to establish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But is this witness aware of that material, because I have seen what you are talking about in the expert report, but not in this witness's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if the witness isn't aware, I'm sure he'll tell us so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Krcmar, you've just told us that it's correct that the bodies were labelled "1/1" through to "1/8."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps at this stage if we could bring up an example of the DNA reports we saw yesterday. And, Your Honours, for ease of using these reports, we've actually removed the reports from the Prosecution's exhibit, which contained a number of documents, and we have the reports as one separate document. It's D593. This is just one document in English, so perhaps it could take up the full screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Krcmar, this was a DNA report that you referred to yesterday, and we can see a name on it: "Radomir Blagojevic."

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And in the box in the top left-hand corner, we can see a number: "br.1/3". Now, what confuses me, Mr. Krcmar, is what you said yesterday in your testimony. You said, in relation to this number, the number "1" indicated the location where the body was found, and the number "3" indicated the number of bones from the body that were sent to the laboratory. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. We misunderstood each other. Number "3" indicates the bag, i.e., all the bones that arrived in that bag. When the bag is opened, the doctors who did that could use that bag to form four or five sub-numbers, which means that they are not certain that the bag contained the bones of only one person. In the Kamenica case, we ended up with 17 numbers, but maybe the best thing would be to have professionals talk about that, i.e., the doctors. I know how things are done, but I'm not a professional in that particular aspect, and I'd rather have the professionals speak about such detailed matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you for that response, Mr. Krcmar. So this is exactly what I wanted to clarify, because what I put to you was the answer you gave to Judge Moloto. But your evidence is the number we can see here, so, for example, the "1/3," what this tells us is this is the third body that was found at that mass grave location? That was the label given to this body; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, at the autopsy, you were present when DNA samples were taken. Could you confirm that a sample was taken from the femur of each body and a sample was taken from the teeth of the skulls that were there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you will allow me, the doctors are the ones who decide where DNA samples should be taken from, from which part of the body. In principle, it is from the skull and from the femur, but it is up to the doctor to decide which bones to use. I was there. I was present. I know how things are done, but I'm not a decision-maker and I can't talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krcmar. Now, on the screen in front of us is an example of one of the DNA reports, and I'd like to ask you about what you had to say concerning the DNA reports. You were asked by the Prosecutor if you saw the signature of the forensic pathologist on the report, and you responded: "On this particular document, there is no signature. This is findings that we received from the DNA laboratory, and the signatures are put on the identification records. This is only a DNA report." Now, as I understood the answer that you gave to the Prosecutor, the DNA report that we see on the screens in front of us does not provide official confirmation that body remains have been identified; and, in order to obtain official verification, you would need to look at the identification records. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And those identification records are entirely different documents which have been signed by an official involved in the DNA analysis process; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This would be an entirely different document. The one that we are looking at is just a working document, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, moving on from there, what I'd like to do is to show you a few pages from the DNA reports to see if you can help us. If you can't answer my questions, then obviously please say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could look at page 2 in this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So here we can see a document that states: "Possible identity, Bozidar Todorovic" -- I beg your pardon, Bozidar Todoric," and we can see a number there, "1/4." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So what we can say is the remains of this body were assigned with the label number "1/4." It was the fourth body to come out of the mass grave; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a bag, a bag marked "number 4."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could please move to page number 4 in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for that, you say it's a bag, but let's just be clear about that. This is a bag containing body remains, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a bag that is used during exhumation to collect mortal remains. Mortal remains are put in the bag, but we cannot be certain that the mortal remains in the bag belong to any one body. One bag can contain remains of two bodies, or you may even have two bags containing remains of just one body. The mass grave had been moved, the bones had been mixed, and that's why the bags are multiple, containing multiple body remains, and it is only after the postmortem that we can be certain. Wherever there's suspicion that the bodies had been mixed, that the bones do not belong to a certain body, a sample is taken and the sample is sent to the DNA laboratory, who then comes back to us with the identification. But I repeat, again, these are very, very expert questions, and you really need to talk to an expert who can give you more information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You may well have preempted my question. I'll put this to you, and if you can't answer it, then I will move on. But here in front of us, we have another document. Again, it states: "Possible identity: Bozidar Todoric," and here we can say these are the remains found in bag "1/7"; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, on the face of it, what we have here, from these reports, is a situation where a person called Bozidar Todorovic -- Todoric is -- his remains are both contained in bag 1/4 and 1/ 7. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes. This is precisely what I was talking about. This means that the bodies were mixed, and it is only when we get the information from the laboratory that we can do what we call "the reassociation" and decide what body is actually in question, but that's the doctor's job.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'm going to move on to the handwritten list that you have referred to during your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And please could we have that document brought up on the screen. It's Exhibit 646.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second. Before you go to 646, Mr. Robson, what do you want done with D593, because D593 is a page you have split out of the previous exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it would be useful as an exhibit, if there's no opposition to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, okay. D593 is admitted as an exhibit. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 649.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Krcmar, we've seen this list contains the details of 51 persons, and we can see from the list that somebody has recorded the names, year of birth, and place of birth on this document. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we just quickly go down the list, we can see that the person who made the list has recorded various names: Number 1, Nedjo Jovic; number 2, Nenad Gligoric; number 3, Slavko Todorovic; and so on. You see that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like to do is bring up a Defence document, D564, which is a document that was disclosed to the Defence by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Krcmar, would you agree with me that what we can see here is a letter addressed to Mr. Daryl Mundis of the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY, dated the 19th of April, 2006?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen this before, but I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we look at the bottom of that page, and if we could go to page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you confirm that this letter comes from Nikola Radovanovic, who is a Minister of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How does he say that when he just said that he doesn't know anything about this letter, and he has seen it for the first time? He can read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can read just like anybody else in the courtroom; but as I've told you, I've not seen this document before. I don't know what comments you are expecting from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Don't worry about that just now, Mr. Krcmar. All I am simply asking you to do is just confirm where the letter is from, or to certainly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He just told you he can read that, he cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Krcmar, you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can go back to page 1 in the English version, please, and see what the document is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Mr. Krcmar, that what the first paragraph of this letter says is: "Dear Mr. Mundis. Please find enclosed information and documents relating to 49 persons. The information was supplied to BiH MoD by the former RS MoD and the Joint Staff of the Armed Forces of BiH in connection with the case number IT-04-83-PT, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic." And we can see at the bottom there that there are also a number of enclosures. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like to turn our attention to is the enclosure -- one of the enclosures with this letter, which can be found at page 3 of the English version and page 2 of the B/C/S. Would you agree with me, Mr. Krcmar, what we can see there is a document dated the 3rd of April, 2006, from the BiH Ministry of Defence, and what it says at the top, in the first paragraph of the document: "With regard to your letter bearing above reference, we received a report from the Chief Staff of RS Army with details of 51 individuals missing or killed." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we could quickly take a look down the list of names in this document, we can see that the first entry is "Nedo Jovic"; the second entry is "Nenad Gligoric"; the third entry is "Savo Todorovic"; and so on. Do you see that, Mr. Krcmar?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that the names on this list are similar to the names that we read out a moment ago on the ABiH list?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, this witness has told us that the names of six bodies have been identified. He was asked to identify those bodies and gave us some information. Now, although it's unclear which of the six remains have been identified, it's important for the Defence to compare some of the entries in this RS Army list with the ABiH handwritten list. So, in order to make that exercise a little simpler, what I'd ask is that hard copies of both the handwritten ABiH list and this RS list be distributed for the courtroom so that we can make that comparison. Before I proceed further, could I please confirm that all the parties have received copies of both the ABiH handwritten list and the RS Army list? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I will not be able to read the RS Army list in Cyrillic, sir. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, what you should find is the English translation is at the rear of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I apologise for not making that clear. Apparently, that's the standard form that the B/C/S is always on top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, yesterday, in your testimony, you were asked about Radomir Blagojevic; and, again, we've seen a DNA report that mentions that name today. What I'd like you to do is take a look at both documents and find entry number 40. So if you go down the RS Army list and the ABiH list, if you could please find entry number 40. Now, if we compare the two entries there, would you agree with me that the name contained within the RS Army list -- if we look at the name contained within the RS Army list, we can see a name there: "Radomir Blagojevic." Is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we look at the ABiH handwritten list, we can see that entry number 40 has a name "Radenko Blagojevic." You'd agree with me that there is a difference between these two names?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a difference. Yesterday, I explained. Please, if I may, if you will allow me to do so, that I reviewed the handwritten list and submitted my revision to the Prosecution. I would like to discuss that latter document. I have not seen this document before, and I would hate to be asked to comment upon something that I have not seen before. I have another list that was matched with the original list, and that second list contains the date of birth, the address of the family, and similar data, and I would really hate to have to comment upon something that I've not been -- seen before. And I know that you have the do I actually compiled, that I compared with the original. I compiled it, and I stand by that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, I would like you to comment on this RS Army list, so you have the opportunity to see what it is. You have the hard copy in front of you. You would agree with me that there was a cover letter which is submitting the list to the Office of the Prosecution. We can see that the list has been prepared by the BiH Ministry of Defence, and then it says: "We received a report from Chief of Staff of RS Army." So this appears to be where this information comes from contained within this list. And if you look at the last page of the list - that would be page 4 of the B/C/S version - we can see that there's a name at the end of the list. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see that, but I've never heard of the person before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, what we're concerned about is the information which is contained -- that we can see in this list. That's what we're really interested in, because we can see that this information provided in the list has come from the RS Army. I've asked you about one of the persons that is purported to have been identified at the mass grave, and I'd like to ask you about a few of the names and a few of the entries contained in these lists. The next person that I'm interested in can be found at entry number 10 in both lists. Could you please find that entry in both documents. So, first of all, dealing with the RS Army list, here information is provided about a person by the name of Bozidar Todoric, and we can see that that person was born on the 14th of January, 1973, in Doboj. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that, but, please, I'm not a member of the Republika Srpska Army. I work at the Office for Missing Persons. And if you want to talk to me, please use the documents of that office, which is a legal institution that deals with searching for missing persons. I stopped working in the army in 1998, and I really cannot comment upon the things that somebody else wrote and signed. There is a document that I submitted to the Office of the Prosecutor which is similar to this list, and I can comment upon that. If you want somebody to comment upon this, please ask the person who compiled this list and who signed it. So I don't know. I can't be sure of anything that's contained in this list. It may be correct, but it also doesn't have to be. So I really wouldn't want to comment on something that I have not seen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, you work for the RS Missing Persons Commission. You were a former member of the RS Army, and you've told us that you get information from many different sources. All I'm simply asking you to do is to take a look at this document, which has come from a high-level authority. It's information that's been provided by the Prosecution to the Defence, and it would seem that you are the appropriate person to deal with this information. Could you please confirm for us that when you compare the entry number 10 in the RS list with the ABiH list, the names are different? In the ABiH list, we can see the name is "Bozidar Todorovic," rather than "Todoric"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those last names are similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The question is: Would you confirm that they are different?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can repeat again, these names to me are similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's possible -- would you agree with me that "Todoric" and "Todorovic" are two different possible surnames that somebody could have in that part of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that when we look at the ABiH list, we can see that the entry for "Bozidar Todorovic" has his date of birth as 1974, rather than 1973 in the RS list?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. It says here: "Bozidar Todorovic, born in 1974 in Doboj."" But if I may, such a person never went missing. A "Todoric" went missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So where we have two different surnames, two different dates of birth, would you agree with me that it's possible that we're talking about two entirely different people? It is possible, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can only discuss one person here, and that is Bozidar Todorovic. Whoever was writing this document wrote down his name incorrectly. We can discuss the similarity between the last names, but we cannot discuss two different last names and two different persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I don't want to get into an argument about this, but it wasn't just his name. It's the date of birth which is different as well. What I'd like you to do is now look at entry number 33 in both lists, please. Do you see in the RS list there an entry for Drago Stjepanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Entry 33, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you see the entry?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, in the RS Army list, we can see it has Drago Stjepanovic's birthplace as Doboj; and if we refer to the ABiH list, we can see that it is given as Maglaj. Those are two entirely different places, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So we have another discrepancy. But of particular significance and what I'd like to ask you about is: We've confirmed, haven't we, that this RS list was prepared in April 2006? That was the day it -- it was sent to the Office of the Prosecution in April of 2006. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And you've told us that the exhumation at the Kamenica grave took place from the 21st to the 23rd of June, 2006; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the last sentence under entry number 33, what it says in relation to Drago Stjepanovic is that: "The body was found and exhumed." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's entry number 33. It's the last sentence within that entry.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that. I've already said that I cannot comment on this document, since it is not mine. I do not stand by it. It wasn't forwarded by my office, and now you're asking me to comment on something that I know nothing about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this entry, which was prepared by the RS Army, suggests that the body of Drago Stjepanovic was found at some stage before April 2006?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, there is no Army of Republika Srpska or the Army of the Federation. It is a joint army. Therefore, after that date, this could not have come from the Army of Republika Srpska. And the second thing is, please, again ask me to comment only on the documents that I sent, rather than having to comment on things I've never seen or know nothing of. The person who signed this document, I don't know who that is. I cannot comment on it. I have the documents which I had forwarded to the Prosecutor, with the index card of each person, with the address. I've already said that, and so as not to waste any time, I can only say yet again that I cannot offer my opinion on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You would agree with me that on the information which the Prosecution has provided, that, on the face of it, Drago Stjepanovic was found and exhumed prior to April 2006, and yet also there seems to be information suggesting that he was -- his remains were discovered in June 2006 as well? How can it be? I take it you have no explanation for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think the witness has explained his position to this question several times. He's told you he cannot comment on a document he doesn't know. He doesn't know why this person who wrote here wrote what he wrote, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I still have a few more names to discuss, but I note the time. So it might be an appropriate time for a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, one of the DNA reports that has been admitted into evidence refers to somebody by the name of Radovan Radojcic. If we can look at entry number 9 on the ABiH handwritten list, can you please confirm that the date of birth given for that person is 1942?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Radovan Radojcic, born in 1942," that's what this document reads in the handwritten one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like another document to be brought up on the e-court screen, please. It's Defence document D595.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, do you agree with me that what we have here is a record of the forensic and criminal/technical examination of dead body remains, prepared by the Office of Tracing Detained and Missing Persons of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And can you confirm that this is the organisation that you work for?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You're familiar with this type of document; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I forwarded this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, if we could look at page 2. First of all, if we could scroll down in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does it have a signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could look at page 2 in the B/C/S version as well, please. If we could please focus on the and close in on the names at the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, do you recognise those names?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could look at page 2 in the English as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm familiar with these names.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the document is signed by, please?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is signed by the forensic specialist, Dr. Zeljko Karan, and a court expert in ballistics, Milko Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just above the names, is right, isn't it, that this document says that: "Using DNA analysis, the skull belonging to the dead body was identified as that of Radovan, father's name Blagoje, Radojcic." You see that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, here, it has his date of birth as the 27th of October, 1956. Would you agree that that is different to what is recorded as the date of birth in the ABiH list?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The difference is in terms of years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This one on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes. I haven't finished with the other one as yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this D595?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: This is D595, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: D595 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 650.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And perhaps if we could return back to the RS Army list on the screen, please, I'm going to deal with the final discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, could you please look at entry number 3 on both the ABiH list and the RS Army list. Could you confirm for us, Mr. Krcmar, that entry number "3" on the RS list refers to somebody by the name of "Savo Todorovic"; whereas, entry number "3" in the ABiH list refers to "Slavko Todorovic"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the handwritten version, it reads "Slavko Todorovic." In this document that you called the document of the Army of Republika Srpska, whereas it was signed by the Ministry of Defence, Joint Staff of the Armed Forces, it reads "Savo Todorovic." If I may, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Mr. Krcmar, that those are two different first names?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Slavko and Savo are two different names; however --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, hang on. If you could please focus on the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. If the witness wants to complete an answer, he's not being allowed to do so. Obviously, he wanted to say something else. I think that he should be allowed to finish his statement -- his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I have given the witness opportunities to give his answer in full on previous occasions; and, essentially, I'm controlling --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're dealing with this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes. So I'm just dealing with specific questions, and I anticipated that the witness was going to go off on a tangent and to a different matter. So I was just merely trying to focus the witness on the question at hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is overruled. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, if you can again look at entry number "3" in the document which the information came from the chief of Staff of the RS Army, I'd like to refer you to the last sentence of that entry. Again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which one is from the Chief of Staff of the RS Army?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the RS Army list, that's what I've been calling it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The one from the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes. But if you look at the first paragraph, it says: "We received a report from the Chief of Staff of RS Army."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It says, "We received ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It's the underneath reference: "With regard to your letter bearing the above reference, we received the report from the Chief of Staff of RS Army."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. The Ministry of Defence received the report from the RS Army, but this letter comes from the Minister of Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Krcmar, in relation to the person named Savo Todorovic, again we can see that according to this list, his body was found and exhumed at some point prior to April 2006; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I wanted to mention. This is incorrect, "Savo Todorovic," and the persons we discussed just a minute ago, "Blagojevic"; and, for the sake of truth, there was another number that we discussed. They were identified on the 29th of November, 2006. This document is the 19th -- is the 3rd of April, 2004. Someone cannot be identified beforehand. I'm trying to say that this document is not valid. The families, on the 29th of November, 2006, identified the bodies. This body was identified as such on that date, and the Prosecution's -- the Prosecutor's office has that information. Again, I must say that this is not a document I can discuss. This was six months after the list that the man was identified. I don't know how this information made its way into this document, but I am not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So what we can say is that according to the material that has been generated relating to these bodies, there are discrepancies, aren't there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You said earlier in your evidence mistakes can be made. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the mistakes had been dealt with. That material is in existence here, and that is what we need to discuss, or rather, that is what I can discuss. I cannot discuss other people's letters and documents that I have nothing to do with.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, you say that you're not able to comment on this document or discuss it, but the fact is that you have been very willing to discuss the ABiH handwritten list, which is also a document that you were not involved in the preparation of. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I said I revised this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before we leave this document that comes from the BiH Ministry of Defence, I'd like to take you through the entries. We have already noted that two of the bodies we've discussed apparently have already been found and exhumed prior -- at some stage prior to April 2006. If I can take you through the list, would you agree with me that according to this document, entry number 2, "Nenad Gligoric," his body was found and exhumed prior to April 2006?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that's what it says here, and a document I cannot comment. This is stated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Number 3, we've just discussed a moment ago. Number 4, "Slobodan Markovic," according to the document, his body was found and exhumed. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall. There is a list of the seven bodies from the Kamenica site that was forwarded. We can discuss that list. Please do not try and trick me into something I know nothing about. Again, to me, this is not a valid document. It is impossible that the date is April 2006. And in item 33 or 30, Drago Stjepanovic -- excuse me, allow me to finish. Drago Stjepanovic, his body was exhumed and found. It is impossible, because his family, on the 29th of November, 2006, signed the identification report. This document is from April. I have no idea what it means. Concerning the documents I handed over, that is what I can discuss. This is a document of the Ministry of Defence, signed by someone I don't know. It seems to me -- it seems to be Mr. Sifet --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It deals with a matter that you have spent a great deal of time looking into and have come here to testify upon. You've also showed willingness to comment upon other documents generated by other army organisations that you were not part of. What I'm asking you to do is just to confirm with me that what we can see on this document is that there were other people who were found and exhumed prior to April 2006. We can see from this list that entry number 4, his body was found and exhumed, wasn't it, according to the list?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you inferred.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 5 --

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Entry number 5, again it appears the body was found and exhumed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragutin Lukic, his body was not found and exhumed. It relates to the photographs of yesterday. He was the last on the right. That person has still not been found. Again, I can only comment on the documents I handed over. I cannot comment on this. I don't know what this is. Give me the photographs back; and, on the photographs, I'll show who Dragutin Lukic is. That person has never been found. I don't know what this thing before me is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You've explained that you don't agree with the contents of this document, but if we can just do this simply. Please, can you confirm that in entry number 7, according to the signed document from the BiH Ministry of Defence, a body relating to entry number 7 was found and exhumed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm anything. We've gone too far. Call the person who signed the document and let him confirm, not me. I've not seen this document before. Yesterday, we spoke about the documents that I'm familiar with, although they originate from other organisations. This is something I've not seen before, and now you're asking me to comment upon it. I am not in a position to comment upon other people's documents, especially documents drafted by the Ministry of Defence. I don't know what this is. Don't ask me to comment upon this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask for this document to please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, I have a difficulty admitting this document into evidence through this witness, who has protested his ignorance of the document so much. He has talked about the contents, but he just has no link to the document. I think you must get a witness that can tender the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the test for admission is that the document should be relevant and have probative value. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Clearly, this list deals with -- it's highly pertinent. It looks as though it was prepared in conjunction with the ABiH handwritten list. The witness has protested that he knows nothing about the contents, but this is a document that has been provided to the Defence by the Prosecution. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is being tendered by the Defence, sir. You see, the Defence has been arguing right through this trial. In fact, just the other day, you were arguing when a witness was being led by the Prosecution, and the witness was commenting on the contents, and the Defence stood up and objected. I confirmed that objection on the basis that there was -- a link was being made between the document and the map. Now, here a link is being made between this document and the other document, but not between this witness and the document. I have allowed you to cross-examine the witness because, yes, I can see the similarities, but I do think you need to get a witness who can authenticate this document. Because if this witness says this document, as he has said so now, this document is not valid, he said so in one of his protests, what should the Court do with it? It can attach no value to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to raise a couple of points, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: First of all, it's been permitted for the ABiH handwritten list to be admitted through this witness, when again this witness has not had anything to do with the preparation and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And this witness said, sir - you'll remember I asked him who generated this list - He said he got the list from the Prosecution or from the Tribunal. He corrected it using his own list. He has seen this document before. He's seeing this document for the first time today. He doesn't know anything about it, but he has said, "Yes, I have seen this document. It's not generated by me, and that is why I could see the mistakes in it. And based on the information that I collected, that I have verified, I corrected the statements."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know when the Defence would have a chance to show this document to the witness prior to cross-examination, so we haven't had the good fortune to do so. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not my point. My point is: You've got to get a witness to tender the document, a witness who can authenticate it, but you can't tender it through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the second point is that this document, the Defence submits, is relevant for credibility, because we've heard testimony from the witness about what happened. We also have his witness statement, and this document, which is from, on the face of it, a high-level official source, provided by the Prosecution, contradicts some of that evidence. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I agree with you entirely, Mr. Robson. If you can understand my point, my point simply is that this witness disavows this document. Therefore, if it goes into evidence, it hasn't been authenticated. We can't even begin to look at it. But if you bring in a witness who can come in and say, "I drafted this document," or, "I authenticated this document, I know about it, I say the contents are true," then we can see. This man says, "No" --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the third point I make, and really this is -- obviously, the Trial Chamber has had it in mind throughout the proceedings to try and save time and move expeditiously, and for the Defence to now attempt to contact a member of the Ministry of Defence to come and testify to this document is going to extend the length of the trial proceedings. And, in connection with that, I would just draw to the Trial Chamber's attention that there didn't appear to be any objection from the Prosecution. I'll be corrected if I'm wrong, but that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There may be no objection, but I think it is the Chamber's responsibility to see to it that proceedings go fairly and even-handed. What is happening today is exactly what happened the other day with a document and a map on the screen here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: There would be a final distinction, a point I would make, a distinction I would draw to Your Honour, and that is: In connection with what happened the other day, where a document was put to the witness and the witness simply stated, "I know nothing about this, I'm not prepared to say anything," this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not what was said last week. A witness was taken through a document and made markings on a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I said to the counsel at that time, "What you are busy doing is establishing a relationship between this document and the map." Now, what you have been busy doing today is establishing a relationship between these two documents, but not a relationship between this witness and this document. This witness disavows this document. He disavows this document completely. He says,"I know nothing about it." He has been saying to you so many times, "Why do you ask me to comment on a document that I know nothing about." And, yes, expeditiousness is a matter to be taken into account. To get a witness to come in here for five minutes to say, "Yes, I know this document, I can vouch for the authenticity of this document," you get tendered, two minutes and he's gone. The Defence is still far from calling its own witnesses. We can mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my final comment on this. The witness, in my respectful submission, has not simply said, "I don't know anything about this document, I'm keeping my mouth closed." He has gone on to refer to the different entries and said, "In respect of this person, they were exhumed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's true. Exactly like the map and the document the other day. He didn't say, "I know nothing about this map." He did point out things. I said to him, I said to counsel, the other day, "Anybody who can read can do what you are doing." Now, anybody who can read these two documents can do what this witness is doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, I'm repeating myself, but we would submit it goes to credibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't dispute that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: -- and the other day credibility was not an issue with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't dispute that. I don't dispute that, but I'm saying tender it correctly. That's all I'm saying. Tender it through the correct witness, not a witness who disavows the document. Find a witness who can tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, at least I'd like it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Let's hear what they have to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just for the record would like to state our objection to the document. Just for the record, we do object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: To what?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: To the admissibility of the document in evidence for the reasons stated. That this witness is -- he's not -- he is repeating just what's in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Sartorio, the issue is: Do you challenge the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I have -- I don't know where it -- yes, that's one other reason. Well, it comes -- it came from the Prosecution, Your Honour, but we disclose everything we receive from whatever source. But, again, he's not from the Department of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I repeat my question. Is this document not an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that question, Your Honour. I think a witness has to make that determination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd just like to note that this list was attached to a cover letter sent to Mr. Mundis. Mr. Mundis has disclosed it, well, through his team, no doubt, disclosed it to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All I'm saying is it is being tendered by the Defence, sir, and I'm saying the Defence must get a witness to tender it. I am prepared to mark it for identification. I'm not precluding it. I just want it to be tendered correctly. Okay. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit MFI 651.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what document did we call it when it came in here, sir? Did it have a "D" number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's D564.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: D564. Thank you so much. Is it Exhibit 651?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI 651.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, 651. Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, at paragraph 27 of your 2007 statement, you say the following: "All this information indicates to me that the skeletons and skull were just thrown into the grave, rather than one full body having been buried intact. This is consistent with information I received from sources, that the large mass grave had been dug up and the bodies reburied in several other graves." Now, I don't want to ask you about what you were told by other people, so I'd be grateful if you could answer this with a "yes" or "no." Is it your assessment that the bodies that were found at the Kamenica grave were initially buried at some other location and then subsequently dug up and moved to the Kamenica grave location?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So this would mean that the burial location at Kamenica was a secondary burial location?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, moving on to the autopsy, in your statement you explained how DNA samples were taken by Dr. Brkic; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In paragraph 29 of your statement, you say: "Dr. Brkic conducted autopsies according to regular procedures. She determined that there were eight bodies and one extra skull. Therefore, to my knowledge, it appears that there were the remains of nine victims." That's in paragraph 29 of your statement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, if I could take you back to what you said a little bit earlier in your statement at paragraph 19, in paragraph 19 you state that: "Dr. Karan concluded that there were possibly ten to 15 bodies in the grave. First of all, just to clarify, Dr. Karan was another forensic expert that was participating at the autopsy that day; is that so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, Dr. Karan was assisting Dr. Brkic. Later on, Dr. Karan re-examined these bodies and established that those were the remains of ten to 15 different bodies. He re-examined those bodies at the request of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So just to go back up to what you've stated, at paragraph 29, you said that: "To my knowledge, there were the remains of nine victims," and that is based on what Dr. Karan has concluded; and then, elsewhere in the statement, you've referred to Dr. Karan concluding there were possibly ten to 15 persons. Are you able to say which was correct? Were there nine remains, the remains of nine persons or the remains of ten to 15?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you. The first postmortem that was done by Dr. Brkic, based on the first preliminary examination, it was established that there were eight or nine bodies. Later on, when the bodies were brought to Banja Luka after the reassociation, Dr. Karan concluded that there were up to 15 bodies. The true findings were confirmed by the DNA laboratory that confirmed that there were 11 bodies in question. You don't have that document, but later on we received confirmation from the DNA laboratory that there were 11 bodies in question here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: This is not contained in any of your statements, is it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This data about 11 bodies is not contained in any of my statements, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You met with Ms. Sartorio on the 22nd of October, some three days ago, in Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not three days ago, actually -- or maybe, yes, I'm sorry. Yes, yes. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And you didn't mention to Ms. Sartorio that 11 bodies had now been -- it was now concluded that there were 11 bodies in the mass grave?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that meeting, we did go through my statement. That's what we did; the existing statement, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, I want to turn to one of the bodies that you mentioned during your testimony and also in your statement. At paragraph 44, you refer to a person on the ABiH list by the name of Obrad Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the Trial Chamber has not seen any evidence that DNA samples were taken from that particular body, and there is no DNA report in respect of that body?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That body was not with the group of bodies in the Kamenica grave, the bodies that were examined as part of this exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: You would agree with me that without official confirmation from the ICMP, there is no real proof as to who that body belongs to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, according to my statement, that the body of this man Petrusic was found, and I'm speaking the truth here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
